# dsh-humanize
English | 简体中文 | Design (Chinese)
> Let reasoning models focus on the work. Let what they deliver read like a person wrote it.
`dsh-humanize` is a plugin for `deepseek-harness`. It targets the machine-sounding jargon that codin
g-specialized models produce on complex tasks.
## Why it exists
Coding-specialized models handle complex engineering reasoning, but their prose drifts toward machin
e jargon. That costs the reader extra effort.
Packing many style and rhetoric constraints into the main prompt splits the model's reasoning attent
ion, and complex tasks get slower.
## How it works
`dsh-humanize` separates logical reasoning from prose polish:
- **Mark at write time**: when content is written, separate code and data from text meant for people

. Only human-facing writes trigger review.
- **One style contract**: `PROSE.md` defines how prose sh

ould read.
- **Cite each rule**: the reviewer annotates against individual `PROSE.md` rules and poin

ts at the expression that violates the rule.
- **Apply later**: review runs in the background while
the main session keeps moving. Staged annotations are applied on demand, and compaction triggers a p
ession keeps moving. Staged annotations are applied on demand, and compaction triggers a polish run.

## Quick reference
| Command | What it does |
| `/humanize [path]` | Polish prose from staged annotations once, then re-review the changed files.

|
| `/humanize-loop [path]` | Polish and re-review in rounds until no annotations remain or the roun

d limit is reached. |
| `/humanize-review [path]` | Review git-tracked files under the path. |
| `/h

umanize-review --changed [path]` | Review files changed since HEAD. |
| `/humanize-review --recent N
[path]` | Review files touched by the last N commits. |
`path` defaults to the session working directory. The `--changed` and `--recent` flags can come befo
re or after the path. Reviews keep only files matched by at least one spec.
## Configuration
Open the dsh-humanize row in the Plugins list and edit its configuration. All settings take effect i
h-humanize row in the Plugins list and edit its configuration. All settings take effect immediately.
### Settings
| Setting | Default | Description |
| `reviewProvider`, `reviewModel` | Session model | Provider and model for review calls, picked from

the host model catalog. |
| `reviewReasoningEffort` | Model default | Reasoning effort for review c

alls, picked from the efforts the model publishes. |
| `mergeProvider`, `mergeModel` | Session model
| Provider and model for polish subagents, picked with the same controls. They apply to every polis

h trigger. |
| `mergeReasoningEffort` | Session effort | Reasoning effort for polish subagents, pick

ed from the efforts the model publishes. |
| `reviewConcurrency` | `3` | Maximum concurrent review c

alls. Minimum 1. |
| `reviewRuleShardSize` | `3` | Maximum rules in each review shard. Minimum 1. |

| `reviewRetries` | `1` | Retries after a failed shard model call. Range 0 to 3. |
| `reviewInterval
Seconds` | `60` | Minimum gap before the next write review, counted from the end of the previous rev

iew. Range 0 to 3600. Set 0 to review immediately. |
| `loopMaxRounds` | `3` | Maximum rounds for `/

humanize-loop`. Range 1 to 10. |
| `saveTurnOutputs` | `false` | Keep the latest main-session respon

se in a system temp file. |
| `mergeOnCompaction` | `true` | Polish prose from staged annotations wh

en context compaction ends. |
| `storageDir` | Empty | Where staged annotations are stored. The defa
ult is `~/.dsh/humanize`. |
The review and polish model sections each have a test button. It sends a minimal request to confirm
the provider, model and reasoning effort respond. Set both fields of a model pair before testing. Du
ring normal calls, a pair with only one field set follows the session model.
### Storage paths
The bottom of the settings page shows where staged annotations, annotation history, review request r
ecords, and final turn outputs are stored. Each path has a copy button.
Relative paths resolve against the process working directory. Changing `storageDir` leaves the old c
solve against the process working directory. Changing `storageDir` leaves the old contents in place.

## Writing specs
### Sources and scope
Specs come from three sources:

- The user-wide spec at `~/.dsh/PROSE.md`.
- Project specs: the direct `.md` children of `.agents/pr

ose/` at the project root. Nested directories are not scanned.
- Directory specs: `PROSE.md` in the
target file's directory and its ancestor directories.
[该节后续省略]
### What enters review
A file enters review when at least one spec applies and the merged set contains at least one numbere
d rule. `include` selects the applicable specs. `priority` and `inherit` only affect merging. There
is no separate review declaration.
Batch collection first drops files that no spec matches. Files matched by a spec without numbered ru
les are reported by the review pipeline. Write review, batch review and post-polish re-review share
ed by the review pipeline. Write review, batch review and post-polish re-review share this decision.
Binary files such as images, archives, fonts and build output skip review. Detection samples the sta
rt of the file. Write review and batch review both use it. A batch review reports how many files it
e file. Write review and batch review both use it. A batch review reports how many files it skipped.
When the model writes a file through the wrapped `write` or `edit` tool, it must declare `human_faci
ng`. Pass true for content meant for people, false for pure code or data. Writes marked true enter r
eview. The rest are skipped. Writes through other tools, such as shell commands, are outside this ch
eck. A programmatic call that omits the field is treated as false and logs a warning.
